name: ransomware_scope_report
description: Put the sealed outputs of an examination side by side and say what they cover and what they do not. It takes outputs by reference, as paths (it imports nothing from the tools that wrote them and runs none): per-host censuses of encrypted_survey (`censuses`), the profile files of encryption_extent (`extents`) and of recovery_validate (`recovery_checks`), timelines (`timelines`: JSON Lines events {host, time, kind}, time an ISO 8601 UTC string ending in Z, kept to microseconds), and a collection recipe's coverage.json (`coverage`: {status, status_basis}), each entry {host, file} (a timeline entry may leave host out when its events carry one). Each census and profile is versioned by the `parser` of its receipt (its last line): `encrypted_survey/3`, `encryption_extent/1` and `recovery_validate/1` are read, and any other version is refused by name; an input with no receipt is read and the answer is partial. It reports, per host: the host and share scope with its DENOMINATORS (the files and bytes in the census, by status, and the candidate share of that host's own census); the bytes inspected by encryption_extent against the bytes in the census (`assessed_against_unassessed`, only for a host that has a census; the two sets of files can differ, and the row says so); candidate findings (the census's candidate files, the extent's high-entropy runs) against validated ones (recovery_validate's `matches_known_original`; a `structurally_valid` file is a candidate, not a validated one); the first and last event of the timeline; and the coverage statements of the collection. For the hosts together it gives a machine-readable `coverage_statement`: the number of hosts, how many have a census, a complete census, a partial census, more than one census (`conflict`) or none (`unknown`), the sums over the hosts that have exactly one census, `extrapolated: false` and `estate_wide_percentage: null`. A host with no census is `unknown`: nothing is said about its files and nothing is extrapolated to it from another host. A host with more than one census is `conflict`: each is shown apart and none is added to the totals. The tool states no estate-wide percentage and no figure it cannot support. A host name is printed through the rule encrypted_survey uses for a path component (its manifest states the shape of an identifier and the rates at which it misses and withholds): a name with an identifier-shaped token is withheld, and every row carries a `host_id` (H1, H2, ...) that is not derived from the name, so that two withheld hosts stay apart; the order of the host rows is the order of the text printed for them, the withheld ones in an order drawn afresh every run. A second check reads every string of the answer and of the files it names on the way out and replaces one that is still identifier-shaped, making a complete answer partial. Aggregation streams: every input is read line by line (a line over 1 MiB is skipped and counted), the sums per host and key are held in memory only up to 20000 keys and then written to a SQLite index `ransomware_scope_report-index-<digest>.sqlite` under the output directory, which holds the aggregates, the inputs with their receipts, the coverage statements and the printing order, and never a row of an input; the answer is read from the index in a deterministic order. At most 100,000 hosts are accepted in one report (more is refused, because the per-host tables are built from the index after the inputs are read and that part has no clock of its own). Memory does not grow with the number of rows: a census of 10,000,000 rows (261 bytes each, 2.6 GB) was read in 76 s at 24 MB resident. The hosts table and the timeline table are paged: rows beyond `limit` (and past about 512 KiB inline) are written whole as JSON Lines and named in pages. A file already there is never replaced, even by a rerun with other limits: the new one takes the next free name (`-2`, `-3`). `status` (also `complete`) is `complete` only when at least one host was found, every input was read to its end, every host has exactly one census that ends in a receipt that says complete, no row was skipped and the time limit was not reached; otherwise `partial` with `status_basis` and `partial_reasons`. The tool's own clock `max_seconds` (default 780, at most 840, below the manifest's 900) is checked before every row and every input; the job's own timeout_seconds is not passed to the tool. It reads only regular files, opened without following a link and without blocking (a named pipe is refused), and writes only under the output directory. A stop signal (SIGTERM, SIGINT, SIGHUP) ends it with one JSON answer (status failed, interrupted, exit code 128 + the signal) after removing the index and the pages it was writing. The handlers are installed when the tool's module code has run as far as its stop block: the start of the interpreter and the compiling of the file come first, and a stop signal in that window can end the tool with no JSON answer at all. SIGKILL cannot be caught: a tool killed that way leaves the hidden temporary files of the index and the pages in tool-output, and, in a window of microseconds, an empty file at a result name; delete them.

censuses.description: Per-host censuses of encrypted_survey: a list of {host, file}, file the path of the census (JSON Lines ending in a receipt with parser encrypted_survey/3). Two entries for one host make that host a conflict

extents.description: Per-host profile files of encryption_extent: a list of {host, file} (receipt parser encryption_extent/1)

recovery_checks.description: Per-host profile files of recovery_validate: a list of {host, file} (receipt parser recovery_validate/1)

timelines.description: Timelines: a list of {host, file} (host optional when the events carry one); file is JSON Lines of {host, time, kind}

coverage.description: A collection recipe's coverage.json per host: a list of {host, file}; the file is JSON with status and status_basis

expected_hosts.description: Host names the report must cover even when no input names them; a host with no census is `unknown`

limit.description: Rows shown inline per table (default 200); every row is counted and a table with more is written whole as JSON Lines and named in pages. The rows shown inline also stop at about 512 KiB whatever limit says

max_seconds.description: The tool's own time limit in seconds (default 780, at most 840; the manifest's timeout is 900). When it runs out no further row is read, what was counted is reported, and the answer is partial
